Lottery winners aren't happier. They're more satisfied.
A famous study from nineteen seventy-eight interviewed twenty-two big winners in Illinois.
They weren't happier than people from the same area.
But twenty-two is tiny. So researchers in Sweden asked over three thousand lottery players, five to twenty-two years after the draw.
Clearly higher. Still there more than a decade later.
Mostly, they felt better about their money.
So winners aren't happier. They just rate their lives higher.
